Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly focuses on national-scale (contiguous United States) spatially explicit land-use and land-cover (LULC) prediction from 2001 to 2051. It implements multiple future scenarios—including two baseline scenarios (1990s trend and high crop demand) and three policy scenarios—and quantitatively compares their outcomes. The modeling uses an econometric approach with spatially resolved inputs (county–soil type combinations) and produces mapped LULC projections (e.g., Figs. 1 and 3). Quantitative outputs include area changes in hectares for major LULC classes, and the methodology details the use of observed land-use transitions (1992–1997 NRI data), endogenous price feedbacks, and a resampled 100-m NLCD 2001 base map. While ecosystem service impacts are analyzed, LULC prediction is the central research objective and methodological foundation, satisfying all core inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.)
